correctness.rationale: All assumptions and quantifiers are explicit. For any degree d>=4 Moore graph, 3-point configurations fall into independent star/nonstar, one-edge, and two-edge-path types. Unique common neighbors give forced 5- and 6-cycle anchors; no triangles/quadrangles force disjoint outside-neighbor sets. Multiplicity polynomials are positive in the same positions and sum to d^2-2. This gives the same enhanced six-bit fourth-vertex support at every move, hence a permanent four-pebble strategy. Repeated vertices and lower-anchor configurations are handled. Rank-three/rank-four formulas distinguish successive degree thresholds. All packaged finite checks were run from the newly authored files; they corroborate but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural extremal graph family has a complete classification at variable widths two, three, and four under unlimited quantifier depth. In particular, a hypothetical degree-57 Moore graph would have precisely the same four-variable noncounting theory as the explicit 50-vertex Hoffman–Singleton graph. The indefinite-depth extension is a meaningful strengthened result beyond a fixed quantifier-rank-four comparison and establishes the exact resource threshold separating the degree-two and degree-three classes.
